claim: Propositional logic provides a complete and decidable formal system for reasoning about truth-functional compounds of propositions using connectives (AND, OR, NOT, IF-THEN)

evidence.title: Classical Logic (SEP)
evidence.finding: Classical propositional logic is sound and complete: every tautology is provable and every provable formula is a tautology, as shown by Post (1921) and others

evidence.title: Mathematical Logic (Ebbinghaus, Flum, Thomas)
evidence.finding: The truth-table method provides a mechanical decision procedure for propositional validity, making it the simplest complete formal system

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Propositional logic is a formal system — its 'correctness' is about internal consistency and completeness, not empirical claims
scoreReasoning.coherence: Sound and complete: truth tables provide a mechanical decision procedure; no contradictions possible in a consistent use
scoreReasoning.convergence: Universal acceptance as the foundation of formal reasoning; intuitionistic logic weakens some rules but accepts the core
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Digital circuits, programming languages, database queries, and all formal verification are built on propositional logic

claim: First-order predicate logic extends propositional logic with quantifiers (for all, there exists) and predicates, enabling rigorous reasoning about properties of objects and mathematical structures

evidence.title: Classical Logic — Predicate Logic (SEP)
evidence.finding: First-order predicate logic is the standard framework for formalizing mathematical theories; it is sound and complete (Goedel 1930) but undecidable (Church-Turing 1936)

evidence.title: A Course in Mathematical Logic (Manin)
evidence.finding: All of modern mathematics can be formalized in first-order logic with set theory axioms (ZFC), demonstrating its expressive power

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Predicate logic is a formal system; its completeness is a proven theorem (Goedel 1930), not an empirical claim
scoreReasoning.coherence: Extends propositional logic conservatively; sound and complete for first-order reasoning
scoreReasoning.convergence: Standard foundation for all of mathematics; higher-order logics exist but sacrifice completeness
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: All mathematical proofs, formal verification, database theory, and AI reasoning systems use predicate logic

claim: Proof by contradiction (reductio ad absurdum) is a valid proof method: if assuming the negation of a proposition leads to a contradiction, the proposition must be true

evidence.title: Intuitionistic Logic (SEP)
evidence.finding: In classical logic, proof by contradiction is valid due to the law of excluded middle; intuitionistic logic rejects this for existential claims but accepts it for refutation

evidence.title: Calculus (Spivak) — Proof Methods
evidence.finding: Proof by contradiction is used throughout mathematics: the irrationality of sqrt(2), infinitude of primes, and Cantor's diagonal argument all rely on it

scoreReasoning.correspondence: This is a rule of inference, not an empirical claim — its validity follows from the law of excluded middle
scoreReasoning.coherence: Logically follows from the law of noncontradiction and excluded middle; provably sound in classical logic
scoreReasoning.convergence: Universal in classical mathematics; intuitionists reject it for proving existence (constructive mathematics) but accept it for refutation
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Essential proof technique in all of mathematics — many fundamental results have no known constructive proofs

claim: Mathematical induction is a valid proof method for establishing that a property holds for all natural numbers: prove the base case and the inductive step

evidence.title: Mathematical Induction (SEP)
evidence.finding: Mathematical induction is equivalent to the well-ordering principle for natural numbers; it is built into the Peano axioms as the fifth axiom (induction axiom)

evidence.title: Analysis I (Tao) — Induction Chapter
evidence.finding: Tao develops all of number theory from the Peano axioms, demonstrating that induction is the essential proof method for establishing properties of all natural numbers

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Mathematical induction is an axiom of the natural numbers (Peano), not an empirical claim — its validity is axiomatic
scoreReasoning.coherence: Equivalent to the well-ordering principle; built into the foundation of number theory and provably sound
scoreReasoning.convergence: Universal acceptance in all mathematical traditions; even constructivists accept induction as a valid proof method
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Induction proofs are ubiquitous in mathematics and computer science — algorithm correctness, data structure properties, combinatorics

claim: Goedel's completeness theorem (1930) proves that first-order logic is complete: every semantically valid formula has a formal proof, and every provable formula is valid

evidence.title: Kurt Goedel (SEP)
evidence.finding: Goedel's 1930 completeness theorem shows that first-order logic is the strongest logic that is both sound and complete — a remarkable justification for its central role in mathematics

evidence.title: Die Vollstaendigkeit der Axiome des logischen Funktionenkalkuels (Goedel 1930)
evidence.finding: Goedel proved that every valid first-order formula is provable from the axioms and rules of first-order logic, establishing the completeness of predicate calculus

scoreReasoning.correspondence: This is a proven mathematical theorem — its truth is established by proof, not experiment
scoreReasoning.coherence: One of the deepest results in logic: syntax (provability) perfectly matches semantics (validity) for first-order logic
scoreReasoning.convergence: Universally accepted; the theorem is a proven fact of mathematics with no dissent
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Justifies the use of formal proof systems for establishing mathematical truth; underpins automated theorem proving

claim: Formal logical systems provide reliable, mechanically verifiable methods for establishing necessary truths and valid inference

evidence.title: Classical Logic (SEP)
evidence.finding: Classical first-order logic, proven sound and complete by Goedel, remains the standard framework for mathematical reasoning and formal verification

evidence.title: Formal Verification in Industry (ACM Computing Surveys)
evidence.finding: Formal logic is used in industry to verify hardware (Intel), software (Microsoft), and safety-critical systems (Airbus), demonstrating its practical reliability

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Logic as a system is not empirically testable — but formal verification using logic produces demonstrably correct hardware and software
scoreReasoning.coherence: Complete, self-contained formal system: propositional logic, predicate logic, proof methods, and completeness form a coherent whole
scoreReasoning.convergence: Universal acceptance of classical logic as the foundation of mathematics; alternative logics exist but extend rather than replace it
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Digital hardware, programming languages, databases, AI, and all of mathematics depend on formal logic
